newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jews in Hebron mourn, Arabs welcome pullback.
newsitem.headline: Jews in Hebron mourn, Arabs welcome pullback.

text.p: Jewish settlers mourned and Palestinians celebrated Israel's handover on Friday of most of Hebron to PLO rule after 30 years of occupation.

Underscoring the volatility of the West Bank town, Palestinians hurled stones and handfuls of produce at Israeli soldiers during a brief confrontation near the Arab market which remains under Israeli control. But no one was hurt.
Both settlers and Palestinians have said they feared for their safety. The town is a flashpoint of Arab-Jewish violence.
"It is a very sad day, a day of mourning," said Noam Arnon, spokesman for the 400 settlers who live in the heart of Hebron's 100,000 Arabs.
At dawn Israel left its military headquarters overlooking the town and Palestinian policemen moved in. In the fifth of the town still held by Israel, soldiers remained to guard settlers.

"I am happy to enter, not as a prisoner, but as a policeman who is liberating this valuable part of the homeland," said Palestinian Preventive Security Chief Jibril Rajoub while inspecting the military headquarters where Palestinians were once jailed but now in charge.
Settlers insisted Hebron was their own, God-given, homeland.
"The people should not give away their homeland and this is a very important part of our homeland," Arnon said.
The settlers opposed the U.S.-brokered accord to hand over parts of the town. Jews, like Moslems, revere the city as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
Palestinians welcomed the long-delayed pullback but said their happiness was muted so long as settlers remained.
"Our joy will not be complete until we see the settlers leave the heart of our city," said Hussein Awaiwi, a 65-year-old Arab resident.

Thirty settler men gathered at Hebron's ancient Jewish cemetery on a hilltop overlooking the city to conduct a ritual mourning ceremony. Each man cut his shirt just below the collar and then tore it. All read from the biblical Book of Psalms.
"It is a very dangerous step for the security of the state of Israel. I am concerned about my safety," Arnon said.
"The conditions have now been created to cause riots and violent demonstrations which could lead to attacks against Jews in the city," he told Reuters.
In 1929 Arab rioters, opposed to rising Jewish immigration and inflamed by sermons at local mosques, massacred 67 men, women and children in the town, then home to some 700 Jews.
In February 1994, settler Baruch Goldstein of the nearby Kiryat Arba settlement massacred 29 Palestinians kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque before survivors beat him to death.
The fate of the Jews in Hebron and in other West Bank settlements will be decided in "final-status" talks between Israel and the Palestinians due to be completed by May 1999.
